title: The minimal mediated sequence cardinality conjecture
statement:
For integers $p$ and $q$ with $0<q<p$, let $N(q/p)$ denote the number of elements in a minimal $(0,p)$-mediated sequence containing $q$. A sequence of integers $A=\{0,q_1,\ldots,q_m,p\}$ is $(0,p)$-mediated if every $q_i$ is the average of two distinct elements of $A$. **Minimal mediated sequence cardinality conjecture.** If $\gcd(p,q)=1$, then

$$
N\left(\frac{q}{p}\right)=\left\lceil\log_2(p)\right\rceil+2.
$$

This extends the elementary formula $N(1/p)=\lceil\log_2(p)\rceil+2$ to all reduced fractions $q/p$; the source states the claim as a conjecture and gives no resolution.
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1906.06179](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.06179).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.07903

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).
source_name: Victor Magron and Jie Wang, “SONC Optimization and Exact Nonnegativity Certificates via Second-Order Cone Programming”, arXiv:2012.07903 (2025).
